knownGaps.rationale: References resolve the same member from line/character-only cursor input, but rename refuses it unless the cursor includes an offset.
TemplateDiagnostics preserves selectedMemberName for the weak owner row, while AppDiagnostics preserves source/domain but drops that selected member identity.

Declare-view-model-member code action edits target a zero-length TypeScript insertion span but publish oldText as null, while other insertion edit plans publish empty-string oldText for all-or-nothing validation.

References correctly enumerate alias usages as usages of the same resource, but primary resource rename currently rewrites alias-tag usages to the new primary name; aliases are independent public registration names and should need an explicit alias operation or remain untouched.
The framework treats <template as-custom-element> as a local custom element with bindables, but cursor info, references, and rename do not surface the local resource at its usage tag.
The framework compiles as-element values through custom-element resource lookup, but cursor info, references, and rename do not dispatch the attribute value as a resource usage.

Value converter tokens are classified and semantic-tokenized, and resource definitions preserve the converter declaration, but cursor info, references, and rename do not join expression converter usages to that resource definition.

Binding behavior tokens are classified and semantic-tokenized, and resource definitions preserve the behavior declaration, but cursor info, references, and rename do not join expression behavior usages to that resource definition.

MultiBindingSegment preserves each target and raw command-bearing name, but TemplateSemanticTokens projects only the enclosing custom attribute plus segment value expressions, omitting all authored segment target and command tokens.

The app registers Aurelia's exported ArrayLikeHandler and the TypeChecker knows ArrayLike<ScopeTask>, but repeatability projection consults only the built-in resolver categories, emits a false AUR0777, and degrades the repeat local to unknown.

The project-local context-scope controller explicitly activates its view with Scope.fromParent(parent, value), but semantic-runtime treats app-owned template controllers as pass-through: the child value binding context is missing and the valid explicit parent lookup silently resolves no symbol, with no open-scope seam.

The app registers an IRepeatableHandler for TaskWindow, but repeat projection ignores the open registration fact, emits a confident AUR0777 and downstream TS18046, and reports complete closure instead of preserving an admitted source with unknown element type.

The parser emits ObjectBindingPattern for repeat.for object syntax, while the checked-in Repeat controller only materializes ArrayDestructuring/ObjectDestructuring and therefore creates no locals. Semantic-runtime currently accepts and types the non-working syntax without a diagnostic.

Once AUR0777 establishes that a repeat source cannot produce runtime rows, child member diagnostics are derivative noise. The diagnostic presentation policy currently publishes both root-cause and downstream local-member failures.

Framework With substitutes an empty object only for undefined; null becomes the child binding context and later scope lookup can throw. Semantic-runtime erases null with getNonNullableType and reports the reachable runtime hazard as clean.

Aurelia's nullable flag changes the runtime coercer wrapper, but semantic-runtime collapses type coercion to setterKind=type-coercion and drops nullable from both BindableDefinition and the public resource row.
CustomAttributeDefinition retains noMultiBindings and template lowering honors it, but SemanticResourceDefinitionRow does not project the policy for MCP, IDE, or future AOT consumers.

The framework accepts set: String as a closed bindable interceptor, but semantic-runtime classifies the global function reference as open through both decorator and static-record metadata while inline function expressions close.

BindableDefinitionField names callback, mode, and set, but convergence only publishes field provenance for name and attribute and the public bindable row has no exact callbackSource, modeSource, or setSource.

Resource definition rows preserve bindable value type and call-signature facts, but SemanticTemplateCursorBindableRow drops them before hover and other cursor consumers can present the selected bindable's type.

Class-level @bindable metadata, its class property, default-derived attribute sites, and child-template usages describe one bindable property, but references choose the decorator string as declaration and omit the TypeScript field.
Inherited static bindable metadata closes to template and attribute usages, but references omit the TypeScript property declaration that the metadata names.
Nearest static bindable references use the broad metadata entry and child-template usage only; they omit the exact name token, class field, and explicit-alias attribute usage.
A static record key and same-named class field are not joined as one bindable property target, so references from the child template omit the metadata key and explicit-alias attribute usage.
Definition-object bindable metadata wins framework merge precedence, but references do not join its exact property-name token to the class field or explicit-alias attribute usage.

Template-origin rename cannot route from a class-level @bindable declaration string to the TypeScript field, so it refuses instead of synchronizing metadata, field, derived attribute, and child-template usage.

Template-origin rename cannot route from static bindable metadata to the named TypeScript field and refuses instead of updating metadata, field, and child-template usage while retaining the explicit alias.
Template-origin rename follows the class symbol and child template but leaves the static bindables record key stale, splitting runtime metadata from the renamed property.
Template-origin rename cannot route from definition-object bindable metadata to the TypeScript field and refuses instead of updating the metadata name, field, and child-template usage.

Template-origin bindable rename updates the derived nameChanged callback, but TemplateRenameFromTypeScript emits only template/attribute edits even though TypeScript rename cannot infer the separate conventional callback symbol.
A TypeScript field rename does not close back to its class-level @bindable metadata, so the semantic propagation query returns no metadata, derived-attribute, or child-template edits.
A TypeScript rename of a field named by inherited static bindables cannot recover the inherited metadata declaration or its default-derived template surfaces.
A TypeScript rename of a field named by nearest static bindables returns no metadata or child-template edits, even though the explicit public alias should remain stable.
TypeScript-origin propagation updates the child template but not the static record key that declares the bindable property, leaving runtime metadata stale.
A TypeScript rename of a definition-object bindable field returns no metadata or child-template edits because the winning bindable declaration is not linked back to the class symbol.

TemplateInlayHints ignores MultiBindingSegment target/raw-name sources and anchors every segment hint to the enclosing custom-attribute name, causing multiple unrelated hints to stack at one position.

The route instruction and route-pattern substrate can close load="route: product-detail" to the product-detail route and its productId parameter, but template completions inside params.bind fall back to binding-scope members instead of projecting route-parameter key candidates.

Aurelia resolves a class routeable through Route.getConfig, so static route metadata should supply the child route's id/path/title/fallback and nested route closure; semantic-runtime currently records the class routeable child with the custom-element resource name path and leaves a matching template load on the root residual endpoint.

A closed dynamic import routeable whose module exports a recognizable custom element should carry resolved resource handles through the promise routeable lane; semantic-runtime preserves the promise/source lane but drops the resolved custom-element identity.

Aurelia RouteConfigContext._friendlyPath is built from the resolved CustomElementDefinition.name, but semantic-runtime RouteConfigContext/RouteContext labels and route-node componentName values are built from the routeable source localName, which is often a TypeScript class name or authored alias.

Aurelia resolves the routeable to a CustomElementDefinition before calling ViewportAgent._handles, so used-by should compare against the resolved custom-element name; semantic-runtime currently compares used-by against routeConfig.component.localName and emits false no-available-viewport-agent issues for CE-name filters.

TemplateDiagnostics projects the AUR3401 router issue with missingInput and a fix-router-instruction suggestion, but the owning AppDiagnostics router row preserves only domain/code/source and drops the repair intent before IDE/custom diagnostic repair affordances are assembled.

TemplateDiagnostics projects the AUR3174 router issue with missingInput and a fix-router-instruction suggestion, but the owning AppDiagnostics router row preserves only domain/code/source and drops the repair intent before IDE/custom diagnostic repair affordances are assembled.
Aurelia IRouteViewModel exposes loaded(...) and does not expose load(...), but semantic-runtime's completion hook vocabulary marks load as router-lifecycle and does not mark loaded.
